The king returned to Naples soon afterwards, and ordered the execution of several hundred French [collaborators](/wiki/Wartime_collaboration "Wartime collaboration"). This stopped only when the French successes forced him to agree to a treaty which included amnesty for members of the French party. When the [War of the Third Coalition](/wiki/War_of_the_Third_Coalition "War of the Third Coalition") broke out between France and the [Austrian Empire](/wiki/Austrian_Empire "Austrian Empire") in 1805, Ferdinand signed a treaty of neutrality with the former. A few days later, Ferdinand allied himself with Austria and allowed an [Anglo-Russian force](/wiki/Anglo-Russian_occupation_of_Naples "Anglo-Russian occupation of Naples") to land at Naples.[[2]](#cite_note-EB1911-2)

[Piastra](/wiki/Neapolitan_piastra "Neapolitan piastra") of Ferdinand IV of [Naples](/wiki/Kingdom_of_Naples "Kingdom of Naples"), dated 1805

The French victory at the [Battle of Austerlitz](/wiki/Battle_of_Austerlitz "Battle of Austerlitz") on 2 December enabled Napoleon to launch an [invasion of the Kingdom of Naples](/wiki/Invasion_of_Naples_(1806) "Invasion of Naples (1806)"). Ferdinand fled to [Palermo](/wiki/Palermo "Palermo") on 23 January 1806, followed soon after by his wife and son, and on 14 February 1806 the French again entered Naples. Napoleon declared that the [Bourbon](/wiki/House_of_Bourbon "House of Bourbon") dynasty had forfeited the crown, and proclaimed his brother [Joseph](/wiki/Joseph_Bonaparte "Joseph Bonaparte") King of Naples and Sicily. But Ferdinand continued to reign over the latter kingdom (becoming the first King of Sicily in centuries to actually reside there) under British protection.[[2]](#cite_note-EB1911-2)

fanoutqa_021142.x:
Women in the United States Senate :: part 03 :: chunk_0002
The first woman to serve in the U.S. Senate was [Rebecca Latimer Felton](/wiki/Rebecca_Latimer_Felton "Rebecca Latimer Felton"); she represented [Georgia](/wiki/List_of_United_States_senators_from_Georgia "List of United States senators from Georgia") for one day as a symbolic gesture in 1922.[[3]](#cite_note-3) Ten years later, [Hattie Caraway](/wiki/Hattie_Caraway "Hattie Caraway") became the first woman to win election to the Senate, representing [Arkansas](/wiki/List_of_United_States_senators_from_Arkansas "List of United States senators from Arkansas"). She first filled the vacancy caused by her husband's death, and then was elected to two full terms.[[4]](#cite_note-4) In 1949, [Margaret Chase Smith](/wiki/Margaret_Chase_Smith "Margaret Chase Smith") began her service in the Senate; she was the first woman to serve in both the [House](/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives") and Senate. Her [1960](/wiki/1960_United_States_Senate_elections "1960 United States Senate elections") reelection bid resulted in Chase Smith winning the nation's first-ever United States Senate election with two female major party nominees. In 1972, [Elaine Edwards](/wiki/Elaine_Edwards "Elaine Edwards") was appointed as the first Catholic woman in the Senate by her husband, the [Governor of Louisiana](/wiki/Governor_of_Louisiana "Governor of Louisiana"), while she was Louisiana's First Lady; she retired after three months. In 1978, [Muriel Humphrey](/wiki/Muriel_Humphrey "Muriel Humphrey") became the first [Second Lady](/wiki/Second_Lady_of_the_United_States "Second Lady of the United States") to serve in the United States Senate, after [Hubert Humphrey](/wiki/Hubert_Humphrey "Hubert Humphrey")'s death in office. [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a2/New_Mexico_population_density_2020.png/250px-New_Mexico_population_density_2020.png)](/wiki/File:New_Mexico_population_density_2020.png)

New Mexico population density map

With just 17 people per square mile (6.6 people/km2), New Mexico is one of the [least densely populated states](/wiki/List_of_states_and_territories_of_the_United_States_by_population_density "List of states and territories of the United States by population density"), ranking 45th out of 50; the population density of the U.S. overall is 90 people per square mile (35 people/km2). The state has 33 counties and 106 municipalities, which include cities, towns, villages, and a [consolidated city-county](/wiki/City-County "City-County"), [Los Alamos](/wiki/Los_Alamos_County,_New_Mexico "Los Alamos County, New Mexico"). Only three cities have at least 100,000 residents: Albuquerque, Rio Rancho, and Las Cruces, whose respective metropolitan areas together account for the majority of New Mexico's population.

Residents are concentrated in the north-central region, anchored by the state's largest city, Albuquerque. Centered in [Bernalillo County](/wiki/Bernalillo_County,_New_Mexico "Bernalillo County, New Mexico"), the [Albuquerque metropolitan area](/wiki/Albuquerque_metropolitan_area "Albuquerque metropolitan area") includes New Mexico's third-largest city, [Rio Rancho](/wiki/Rio_Rancho,_New_Mexico "Rio Rancho, New Mexico"), and has a population of over 918,000, accounting for one-third of all New Mexicans.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/61/Portret_van_Robert_Boyle%2C_RP-P-OB-4578_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Portret_van_Robert_Boyle%2C_RP-P-OB-4578_%28cropped%29.jpg)](/wiki/File:Portret_van_Robert_Boyle,_RP-P-OB-4578_(cropped).jpg)

[Robert Boyle](/wiki/Robert_Boyle "Robert Boyle"), who discovered the reaction between [iron filings](/wiki/Iron_filings "Iron filings") and dilute acids

In 1671, Irish scientist [Robert Boyle](/wiki/Robert_Boyle "Robert Boyle") discovered and described the reaction between [iron](/wiki/Iron "Iron") filings and dilute [acids](/wiki/Acid "Acid"), which results in the production of hydrogen gas.[[63]](#cite_note-63)[[64]](#cite_note-64)
Boyle did not note that the gas was flammable, but hydrogen would play a key role in overturning the [phlogiston theory](/wiki/Phlogiston_theory "Phlogiston theory") of combustion.[[65]](#cite_note-Ramsay-1896-65)

In 1766, [Henry Cavendish](/wiki/Henry_Cavendish "Henry Cavendish") was the first to recognize hydrogen gas as a discrete substance, by naming the gas from a [metal-acid reaction](/wiki/Metal-acid_reaction "Metal-acid reaction") "inflammable air". He speculated that "inflammable air" was in fact identical to the hypothetical substance "[phlogiston](/wiki/Phlogiston_theory "Phlogiston theory")"[[66]](#cite_note-66)[[67]](#cite_note-cav766-67) and further finding in 1781 that the gas produces water when burned. He is usually given credit for the discovery of hydrogen as an element.[[10]](#cite_note-Nostrand-10)[[9]](#cite_note-nbb-9)

fanoutqa_000150.x:
Star Wars: Episode III – Revenge of the Sith :: part 02 :: chunk_0001
Lucas began writing the script before production of *Attack of the Clones* ended, saying he wanted the end of the trilogy to be similar to a romantic tragedy, thus leading into Darth Vader's state at the beginning of the next film. Production of *Revenge of the Sith* started in June 2003, and filming took place in Australia, Thailand, Switzerland, China, Italy, and the United Kingdom.

*Revenge of the Sith* premiered on May 16, 2005, at the [Cannes Film Festival](/wiki/Cannes_Film_Festival "Cannes Film Festival"), and was theatrically released in the United States on May 19. The film received mostly positive reviews from critics, with praise for the mature themes, darker tone, emotional depth, soundtrack and action sequences, although some criticism was reserved towards Lucas's screenplay; most consider it the best installment of the prequel trilogy. It broke several box-office records during its opening week and earned $850 million worldwide during its initial run, making it the second-highest-grossing film in the *Star Wars* franchise at the time. It was the highest-grossing film in the U.S. and the [second-highest-grossing film worldwide](/wiki/2005_in_film#Highest-grossing_films "2005 in film") in 2005. It also holds the record for the highest opening-day gross on a Thursday, at $50 million. It was the last *Star Wars* film distributed by [20th Century Fox](/wiki/20th_Century_Fox "20th Century Fox"), although the company (and, by extension, the film) was [acquired by Disney](/wiki/Acquisition_of_21st_Century_Fox_by_Disney "Acquisition of 21st Century Fox by Disney") several years after it acquired [Lucasfilm](/wiki/Lucasfilm "Lucasfilm"). It also serves as Lucas' most recent directorial credit.
